advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm holding the deploy flock for up to MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT during a no-op self-heal tick is acceptable, or bound the wait separately from the deploy readiness deadline.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:979: self-heal runs inside the `if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]` no-op branch
advisory.finding: mcp_wait_health_contract blocks the tick for up to MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT (default 120s) inside the no-op / up-to-date branch, holding the deploy flock for the whole wait during what is otherwise a fast no-op tick.
scenarios: A slow-starting restarted backend keeps the no-op tick (and its flock) held for up to 120s per attempt.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the docker `port` stub return empty for exited containers and add a `docker inspect HostConfig.PortBindings` stub, then assert self-heal still identifies and restarts the exited live backend.
evidence: Commit message: 'an exited live backend can report no mapping there; fall back to HostConfig.PortBindings so the self-heal watchdog can map nginx's live port back to the stopped container'

Docker stub `port` case returns the mapping unconditionally: `port) echo "127.0.0.1:$(port_of "$2")"; exit 0 ;;` (test file line 105) — it does not check container state, so `docker port` never returns empty for an exited container and the fallback is dead in the tests.
search_files for 'PortBindings' under tests/scripts returned (no matches).
advisory.finding: The newly added HostConfig.PortBindings fallback in mcp_port_of (autodeploy.sh:497-502) — which the commit message states the fix depends on to map an EXITED live backend back to its container — is never exercised, because the docker stub's `port` case echoes the mapping regardless of container state. The tests would still pass if the fallback branch were deleted or broken.
scenarios: An exited managed container whose `docker port 8091/tcp` reports nothing but whose HostConfig.PortBindings still records the 8091 mapping — exactly the case self-heal must handle.
advisory.suggested_fix: Teach the docker stub to emit no mapping from the `port` case when state_of "$2" != running, and to answer the `HostConfig.PortBindings` inspect format from the seeded port, so mcp_port_of's fallback branch is actually driven.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate mcp_self_heal_live_backend on `mcp_backoff_active` (skip while the mcp backoff window is open) so a persistently-dead backend honors the exponential throttle it records.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1180: `if mcp_backoff_active && mcp_delta; then` (the normal mcp path DOES gate on backoff)
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:933: self-heal failure path `    record_mcp_backoff_failure` writes MCP_BACKOFF_FILE but no self-heal call site ever consults mcp_backoff_active before retrying
blocking.finding: mcp_self_heal_live_backend is invoked unconditionally at both call sites and never checks mcp_backoff_active, so the exponential mcp backoff it schedules via record_mcp_backoff_failure is never honored: a persistently-dead live backend retries docker start (and the up-to-120s health wait) on every ~2-minute no-op tick, defeating the throttle the backoff file is meant to enforce.
scenarios: Live MCP backend stays dead (e.g. image crash-loops on start); every timer tick re-runs docker start and blocks up to MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, ignoring the backoff wait just scheduled.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where docker start succeeds but the health contract never passes (health-8092='DOWN'), asserting rc!=0 and mcp-deploy-backoff exists.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:932-939: `if ! docker start "$name" ...; then record_mcp_backoff_failure; return 1; fi` followed by `if ! mcp_wait_health_contract "$live"; then record_mcp_backoff_failure; return 1; fi`
test stub only models start failure: `[ -f "$DS/start-fails" ] && exit 1` (test file line 127)

Named violating input: seed exited rebar-mcp-live-8092, leave start-fails UNSET (start succeeds) but write health-8092 = 'DOWN' so mcp_wait_health_contract never passes; the added health-fail gate (lines 936-939) must record MCP backoff and exit 1, and this path is asserted by no test.
blocking.finding: No test covers the restart-succeeds-but-health-contract-never-passes branch of mcp_self_heal_live_backend (autodeploy.sh:936-939). test_dead_live_mcp_backend_heal_failure_is_retryable only injects a `docker start` failure (start-fails); it never exercises the second failure gate where `docker start` succeeds but `mcp_wait_health_contract` times out, which must also call record_mcp_backoff_failure and return 1.
scenarios: A restarted live backend comes back up but fails its /health contract (store missing / handshake failed / never reachable within MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT).
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test cloning test_dead_live_mcp_backend_heal_failure_is_retryable but instead of start-fails, write health-8092 as 'DOWN' (or a store-missing/handshake-failed body); assert `start rebar-mcp-live-8092` in cmds, returncode != 0, and mcp-deploy-backoff exists.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with TARGET != DEPLOYED and a dead live backend asserting the deploy-path self-heal (line 986) restarts it and gates the deploy on failure.
evidence: All three new tests seed `(mcp_box["state"] / "deployed-sha").write_text(_TARGET + "\n")`, forcing TARGET==DEPLOYED and the line-979 no-op branch (test file lines 909, 934, 964).

Named violating input: leave deployed-sha at _DEPLOYED (so TARGET != DEPLOYED, main advanced), seed exited rebar-mcp-live-8092 owning the live upstream port; the line-986 self-heal must restart it during the deploy tick, and no test covers this call site.
blocking.finding: No test drives mcp_self_heal_live_backend on the source-advancing deploy path (autodeploy.sh:986). All three new tests set deployed-sha == _TARGET, exercising only the no-op call site at line 979; the newly added `mcp_self_heal_live_backend || exit 1` at line 986 (which must run — and abort the deploy on failure — when TARGET != DEPLOYED) is never executed.
scenarios: main advanced (a real deploy tick) while the live MCP backend is dead — the second, deploy-path self-heal invocation.
